main_text.head: LXVIII. ELECTORI SAXONIÆ
Illustrissime & Celsissime Princeps.
main_text.p: 26. DIe May scripseram ad Celsitudinem V., sed cum minister meus in superiorem Saxoniam pervenisset, intellexit Celsitudinem V. valetudinis curandæ causa ad fontem acidum Swalbachicum contendisse. Dissessi igitur quam primum Brema, ut Celsitudinis V. redituri obviam irem, sed ex Illustrissimo Landtgravio rescivi Celsitudini V. per valetudinem non licere ante aliquot dies itineri se committere. Idcirco operæ pretium esse duxi, ut me conferrem ad Illustrissimum Ducem Joh. Casimirum Palatinum; quo

page.notes: The page number reads "35" followed by a worn mark, possibly a flourish or damage; I have given it as 35. Several words in the text are set in italic and are marked as such, but the scan is faint, so the italic boundaries are approximate. The paragraph text ends at the page foot with the catchword "quo", as printed; the line "Dissessi" may be a printing form of "Dissessi" (I have copied it as seen). Some words near the right margin are partly obscured by specks, e.g. "Celsitudini" and "Dissessi", which are read with reasonable but not complete certainty.
